extracted.subtask_description: Formal definitions and preservation results for satisfaction, truth, definability, logical implication, homomorphisms, and elementary classes in first-order logic. Targets understanding when formulas/sentences are true in structures and how structure mappings affect truth and definability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of satisfaction (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: |=A ϕ[s] — A satisfies a wff ϕ with assignment s: V → |A| iff the translation of ϕ determined by A, where each free variable x is translated as s(x), is true. Satisfaction is defined formally by recursion on the structure of terms and formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives an informal version and then a formal recursive definition broken into clauses for terms, atomic formulas, connectives, and quantifiers. Emphasize that the notion is mathematical (no English translation needed) and relies on recursion/unique decomposition of wffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of assignment to terms
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a unique extension s : T → |A| of the assignment s: V → |A| to all terms, defined recursively: (1) s(x)=s(x) for variables, (2) s(c)=c^A for constants, (3) s(f t1...tn) = f^A(s(t1),...,s(tn)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence and uniqueness follow from the recursion theorem and unique decomposition of terms. Notation t^A[s] (or s(t)) makes dependence on A and s explicit. This extension is used throughout the satisfaction clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of atomic formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: |=A = t1 t2[s] iff s(t1) = s(t2). For an n-place predicate parameter P: |=A P t1 ... tn[s] iff (s(t1),...,s(tn)) ∈ P^A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality is treated as a logical symbol (not a parameter). Atomic clauses are explicit (not recursive). Examples in the text illustrate checking atomic satisfaction in concrete structures (e.g., (N; ≤, S, 0)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursive clauses for connectives and quantifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: For wffs built inductively: (i) |=A ¬ϕ[s] iff not |=A ϕ[s]. (ii) |=A (ϕ → ψ)[s] iff either not |=A ϕ[s] or |=A ψ[s] (i.e., if A satisfies ϕ with s then A satisfies ψ with s). (iii) |=A ∀x ϕ[s] iff for every d ∈ |A|, |=A ϕ[s(x|d)] (where s(x|d) changes s only at x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the formalizations of ¬, →, and ∀. The clause for ∃ is given via equivalence with ¬∀¬. The recursion theorem again justifies these clauses; see text for alternative function-based formulation (h(ϕ) sets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence of satisfaction only on free variables (Theorem 22A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If s1 and s2 agree on all variables that occur free in ϕ, then |=A ϕ[s1] iff |=A ϕ[s2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on ϕ following the recursive definition of satisfaction. Consequence: for sentences (no free variables) the choice of s is irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth of sentences (Corollary 22B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sentence σ, either (a) A satisfies σ with every function s: V→|A|, or (b) A does not satisfy σ with any such s. If (a) holds we say σ is true in A (write |=A σ) or A is a model of σ; if (b) holds σ is false in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures the notion of a sentence being true in a structure (model). For sets of sentences, A is a model of the set iff it is a model of every member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of logical implication
rubrics_metrics.description: For a set Γ of wffs and a wff ϕ: Γ |= ϕ iff for every structure A and every s: V→|A| such that A satisfies every member of Γ with s, A also satisfies ϕ with s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same |= symbol used previously for tautological implication but now reserved for logical implication in first-order logic. For sentences Γ and τ, Γ |= τ iff every model of Γ is also a model of τ (Corollary 22C). Examples of implication/nonequivalence are provided in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity (valid formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: A wff ϕ is valid iff ∅ |= ϕ (written simply |= ϕ). Equivalently, ϕ is valid iff it is true in every structure (and every assignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validity is the first-order analogue of sentential tautology. The text notes the complexity difference between checking tautologies (finitary) vs validity (ranges over all structures) and remarks on decidability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definability of relations in a structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Given A and a formula ϕ whose free variables are among v1,...,vk, the k-ary relation defined by ϕ in A is {(a1,...,ak) | |=A ϕ[[a1,...,ak]]}. A k-ary relation on |A| is definable in A iff some formula defines it there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in (N; 0,S,+,·) the ordering, singletons {n}, primes, and exponentiation are definable (with proofs or references). The complexity of a definable relation relates to complexity of simplest defining formula; many decidable/effectively enumerable relations are definable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary class / definability of classes of structures
rubrics_metrics.description: A class K of structures is elementary iff K = Mod τ for some sentence τ. K is elementary in the wider sense (EC) iff K = Mod Σ for some set Σ of sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: class of all graphs, directed graphs, groups, fields are elementary; class of finite graphs is not elementary. The text gives examples and shows how to form Σ to characterize properties like 'infinite groups' (using sentences λ_n 'there are at least n things').

rubrics_metrics.name: Homomorphism (strong homomorphism) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A homomorphism h: |A|→|B| satisfies: (a) for each n-place predicate P and tuple a1..an, (a1..an) ∈ P^A iff (h(a1)..h(an)) ∈ P^B; (b) for each n-place function symbol f, h(f^A(a1..an)) = f^B(h(a1),...,h(an)). For constant c this yields h(c^A)=c^B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors call these 'strong homomorphisms'. If h is one-to-one it is an isomorphism (an isomorphic embedding). If ran(h)=|B| and h is bijective onto |B| it is an isomorphism onto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substructure and closure conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given B and nonempty A⊆|B| closed under all functions f^B, there is a unique substructure of B with universe A (predicates/functions/constants are restrictions). Conversely, identity map is isomorphism of A into B iff predicates/functions/constants of A are restrictions from B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure under function symbols is necessary for being a substructure (includes constants). If language has no function symbols, any nonempty subset gives a substructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homomorphism theorem (preservation under homomorphisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let h be a homomorphism of A into B and s map variables into |A|. (a) For any term t, h(s(t)) = (h ◦ s)(t). (b) For any quantifier-free formula α not containing equality: |=A α[s] iff |=B α[h◦s]. (c) If h is one-to-one, (b) holds also with equality allowed. (d) If h is onto, then (b) holds even with quantifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on terms/formulas. Consequences: quantifier-free properties are preserved under homomorphisms; isomorphisms preserve all formulas; onto homomorphisms preserve satisfaction of quantified formulas as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary equivalence and isomorphism implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Two structures A and B are elementarily equivalent (A ≡ B) iff for any sentence σ, |=A σ iff |=B σ. Isomorphic structures are elementarily equivalent (A ∼= B ⇒ A ≡ B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, elementarily equivalent structures need not be isomorphic (example: (R,<) ≡ (Q,<) though different cardinalities). The textbook discusses building elementarily equivalent but non-isomorphic structures via compactness/other results later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphisms preserve definable relations (Corollary 22E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If h is an automorphism of A and R is an n-ary relation definable in A, then for any a1,...,an ∈ |A|, (a1,...,an) ∈ R iff (h(a1),...,h(an)) ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: let ϕ define R in A; apply the homomorphism theorem to get equivalence of |=A ϕ[[a1,...,an]] and |=A ϕ[[h(a1),...,h(an)]]. Use automorphisms to show non-definability by exhibiting an automorphism that moves some element(s) while preserving structure (examples: h(x)=x^3 in (R,<) shows N not definable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decidability/complexity remark about validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike propositional tautologies (decidable by finitely many truth assignments), to check first-order validity one must consider every structure A and every assignment s; hence the set of valid wffs fails to be decidable (see Section 3.5), though it is effectively enumerable via equivalence with deducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explanatory remark connecting semantic definition of validity to later metatheorems (completeness, enumerability). The text warns about the increased complexity of first-order validity vs sentential tautologies.
